Its 24 outcomes vary initial values, shared/distinct objects, inherited interfaces, checked cross-interface casts and nil receivers. The statically typed Pascal counterpart checks independent ordinary/IA/IB/child property implementations, aliases, default indexing, compound writes, constant and computed readers, statement writers, global data and returned functions retaining Self. The source grammar in Parsers/PascalABCParserNewSaushkin/ABCPascal.y:2188-2224 distinguishes bare field/method accessor identifiers from reader expressions and writer statements. SemanticRulesForYacc.cs:623-633 creates a reader function or a writer procedure with a value parameter. TreeConverter/TreeConversion/syntax_tree_visitor.cs:4614-4631 requires a bare reader identifier to name a class field or method; a global expression must use expression syntax, such as read (Global). Native analysis retains that distinction. It allocates closed synthetic signatures first and binds expression/statement bodies after global declarations, allowing forward property references with no runtime evaluation or name lookup.

Explicit properties occupy separate class/interface maps. Exact child qualifiers precede inherited candidates, and ordinary class property lookup does not expose explicit names or default indexers. Existing field/method accessors retain exact type/index signatures. Expression readers and statement writers use normal VM frames and preserve property parameter names, the setter value parameter, Self and closure lifetimes. This adds no TypeInfo, Cell, Value or VM frame fields, and keeps the normal Windows stack size and existing outlined generator handlers.
